plan.topic: Headache since starting orforglipron (Foundayo)? Headache is on the US label's common list
plan.angle:
Sentence 1: 'Headache since starting Foundayo, orforglipron? It's on the label's common list.'
- Optional stat: 'About 9 in 100 at the highest label dose had headache, versus 7 in 100 on placebo.'
- Card scope: 'Foundayo US label, pooled Trials 1 and 2: adults with obesity or overweight plus a weight-related condition, with or without type 2 diabetes'.
- If space is tight, use the label wording only and no number.
- Keep the tips, the pharmacist line, the emergency headache line and the fixed don't-stop line as briefed.
plan.why: Spin-off of L1. It pairs an approved drug name with a felt symptom, our strongest Short signal (Foundayo nausea 833 views, Foundayo Thanksgiving 896), and sends viewers to the Foundayo long video. | fact-check: Headache is confirmed on the Foundayo PI (rev July 2026) Table 1 common list: 9% at the highest label dose vs 7% on placebo. But Table 1 pools Trials 1 and 2, and Trial 2 enrolled adults with type 2 diabetes. So the briefed population ('Trial 1, adults without diabetes') is wrong for this stat. The difference vs placebo is small (2 percentage points), so don't frame headache as caused by the drug. The brief already says not to name a cause.

package.title: Orforglipron (Foundayo) and Headache: What the Label Shows #shorts
package.description:
Headache since starting orforglipron (Foundayo)? It's on the label's common list: about 9 in 100 on the top label dose (17.2 mg) vs about 7 in 100 on placebo, in adults with obesity or overweight, up to 72 weeks.
A headache that comes on suddenly and is extremely painful: call your emergency number right away. For anything that isn't that emergency sign, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.
#orforglipron
Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

factcheck.summary: The Short is accurate and safe. I checked both sources. In the Foundayo US label (rev 7/2026), section 6.1 Table 1 pools Trials 1 and 2 (up to 72 weeks; 3,155 adults with obesity or overweight, with or without type 2 diabetes). It lists headache at 9% on 17.2 mg (also 9% on 9 mg, 8% on 5.5 mg) vs 7% on placebo, so "about nine in a hundred on the highest label dose… on placebo, about seven" is correct, and calling the gap small is fair. The NHS Headaches page (last reviewed 17 April 2024) supports "drink plenty of water" and "do not skip meals". It also says to call 999 for a headache that "started suddenly and is extremely painful", which is close to the script's emergency line. The script makes no claim about cause, the fluid caveat is there, the painkiller step sends people to a pharmacist with no dosing, and the safety, don't-stop and loop lines are worded correctly. There is no subscribe line or "link in the description". The word count is 112, inside the tight arm. Two small on-screen fixes are below: they are muted-viewer polish, not accuracy errors.

issues.claim: Headache: 9 vs 7 in 100 (Foundayo 17.2 mg vs placebo)
issues.problem: The stat card leaves out the population and the timeframe (the stat_label has the weeks but no population). Our muted-viewer rule says every stat card names both.
issues.fix: on_screen_text: "Headache: 9 vs 7 in 100 (Foundayo 17.2 mg vs placebo, adults with obesity or overweight, up to 72 weeks)"; stat_label: "Headache: Foundayo 17.2 mg vs placebo, adults with obesity or overweight, with or without type 2 diabetes, up to 72 weeks"

issues.claim: Headache since starting Foundayo? It's on the label's common list
issues.problem: The opening card drops the spoken hedge "the gap with placebo is small". Without it, a muted viewer may read the card as saying the drug causes the headaches.
issues.fix: "Headache since starting Foundayo? It's on the label's common list, and the gap with placebo is small."
